:::{#def-infinite-sum}
#### Infinite sum (series)

Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots$ be a sequence in $[0, \infty]$,
with partial sums $s_n$ (@def-partial-sum).
The **infinite sum** (also called a **series**)
$\sumto{i}{\infty} a_i$ is the limit of the partial sums:

$$\sumto{i}{\infty} a_i \eqdef \lim_{n \to \infty} s_n$$

Here the limit is a real number
when the partial sums are real numbers that [converge](algebra.qmd#def-sequence-limit) to it,
and it is $\infty$
when the partial sums [diverge to $\infty$](algebra.qmd#def-sequence-limit)
or some partial sum is $\infty$;
@lem-nonneg-series, next, shows that one of these always happens.
Sums with other index ranges, such as $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k$,
are defined the same way.

:::
